source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Adults may inject once daily at any time of day while following prescribed missed-dose instructions","B":"Adults must inject at exactly the same time each day or the basal insulin becomes unsafe to use","C":"TRESIBA is a rapid-acting mealtime insulin that should be administered before every meal","D":"Adults and children should both vary injection time freely from day to day without a schedule"}}
source_row.rationale: The current TRESIBA label states that adults inject once daily at any time of day, while pediatric patients should inject once daily at the same time every day. Adult timing flexibility therefore should not be generalized to pediatric dosing.
source_row.source_detail: Section 2.2 General Dosing Instructions: adults inject once daily at any time of day; pediatric patients inject once daily at the same time every day.
source_row.stem: An adult client is prescribed insulin degludec (TRESIBA) once daily and asks whether every dose must be given at exactly the same clock time. Which teaching is correct?
